headline: EQUINOX GOLD Q2 176,836 oz — GREENSTONE + VALENTINE DELIVER RECORD CANADIAN OUTPUT, +11% QoQ (TSX:EQX)
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) reported July 10 that Q2 2026 consolidated gold production reached 176,836 ounces — including a combined 97,273 ounces from its Greenstone and Valentine mines in Canada, where output increased 11% quarter-on-quarter. The Canadian production milestone arrives weeks before the July 22 shareholder vote on the $18.5-billion combination with Orla Mining, meaning the pro-forma production from a combined entity at $4,100+ gold would represent the strongest earnings quarter in either company's history. With ISS already endorsing the deal and both boards unanimous, the Q2 production figure is the operational proof-point behind the strategic rationale: Equinox's Canadian flagship mines are performing at exactly the cadence needed to absorb the complexity of a transformational merger.

headline: SILVER $59.57 FACES MAKE-OR-BREAK JULY 14 CPI — 63% SEPTEMBER HIKE ODDS CAPPING SAFE-HAVEN BID
snippet: Silver edged lower to $59.57 on July 10 despite persistent Middle East tensions — a notable divergence from silver's historical safe-haven behaviour — as markets priced a 63% probability of a September Federal Reserve rate hike. The mechanism is identical to the one suppressing gold: Iran escalation drives crude higher, crude lifts CPI expectations, elevated CPI expectations keep the Fed hawkish, dollar strength pressures non-yielding metals. Monday's July 14 CPI print is the single catalyst that could reverse this: a sub-3.8% reading collapses September hike probability and reopens silver's upside case, while 4.0%+ extends the correction from January's $121.60 high — a 51% retracement already. The silver market is running its sixth consecutive structural supply deficit in 2026, China reclassified silver as a strategic material requiring export licenses on January 1, and the long-run demand case from green technology and monetary hedging is intact; the question is whether macro headwinds lift long enough for the structural bid to reassert before the CPI verdict.

headline: ATHA ENERGY DRILLS 37m COMPOSITE URANIUM — WIDEST RIB NORTH HIT TO DATE, 300m STRIKE CONTINUITY CONFIRMED (TSXV:ATHA)
snippet: ATHA Energy Corp. (TSXV: ATHA) reported July 9 that drill hole RIBN-DD-003 at the Rib North Discovery within the 100%-owned Angilak Uranium Project in Nunavut intersected 37 metres of total composite uranium mineralization across 15 zones — the widest single intersection at the discovery to date — while a secondary east-west mineralized structure was confirmed approximately one kilometre from the primary Rib corridor via hole RIBN-DD-008, which returned 14 metres across nine zones from 398 to 646 metres depth. The 2026 Angilak program, the largest ever on the project at approximately 20,000 metres across three rigs, has now outlined mineralization continuity over 300 metres along strike from the maiden discovery hole. Mineralization is basement-hosted vein-type uranium with albite, hematite, graphitic and sulphide structures — geologically analogous to the world-class Athabasca Basin basement-hosted deposits. Outside the Basin but presenting with the same style, Angilak is emerging as a district-scale uranium system: if strike continuity extends past 500 metres with consistent widths, a maiden resource estimate becomes a realistic near-term objective.

headline: ANDINA COPPER CONFIRMS PORPHYRY DISCOVERY: 468m @ 0.50% Cu INCL. 164m @ 0.70% Cu AT PIUQUENES NORTH (TSXV:ANDC)
snippet: Andina Copper Corp. (TSXV: ANDC, OTC: PMMCF) reported July 8 that initial discovery drilling at the Piuquenes North target in San Juan Province, Argentina returned drillhole PIU13 intersecting 468 metres at 0.50% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au, 3.04 g/t Ag from 700 metres depth — including a 164-metre high-grade core at 0.70% Cu, 0.44 g/t Au, 4.19 g/t Ag from 924 metres — confirming the discovery of a new multiphase porphyry copper-gold system tested for the first time via a large discrete MT (magneto-telluric) geophysical target identified in the 2026 survey. Companion hole PIU12 returned 14 metres at 0.38% Cu from 864 metres. A 468-metre intersection grading 0.50% copper in a first-drill porphyry discovery anywhere in the Western Andean corridor is a material result: at $6.24/lb copper, a system with confirmed 1,168-metre vertical extent, a strong gold credit, and proximity to Andina's established Piuquenes East discovery represents one of the more significant new copper-gold porphyry confirmations in the Argentine Andes this cycle — and the next drill test will determine whether grade continues to improve at depth.

headline: MINAURUM QUINTERA VEIN: 5.95m @ 1,117 g/t AgEq — EUROPA SUR 882 g/t, ALAMOS NOW AT 6 DRILL RIGS (TSXV:MGG)
snippet: Minaurum Silver Inc. (TSXV: MGG) reported July 8 continued high-grade drill results from its 50,000-metre Phase II resource-expansion program at the Alamos Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico — including hole AL26-215 returning 5.95 metres at 1,117 g/t silver equivalent (including 2.40 metres at 2,557 g/t AgEq) from the Quintera vein zone, and the Europa Sur vein returning 3.20 metres at 882 g/t AgEq including 0.95 metres at 2,423 g/t AgEq. The program has now expanded to six rigs as Minaurum accelerates conversion of Alamos's multiple high-grade vein zones into a maiden resource estimate. At $59/oz silver, a 1,117 g/t intersection represents nearly 19 times the spot silver price in contained metal per tonne of rock — making this one of the highest-grade active silver exploration programs currently drilling anywhere in Mexico. Multiple vein zones remain open at depth and along strike, meaning the eventual resource base will likely span the full multi-vein architecture of the district.

headline: AURA MINERALS Q2 75,437 GEO FROM 6 MINES — 18% ABOVE Q2 2025 AS MULTI-COUNTRY PLATFORM HITS STRIDE (TSX:ORA)
snippet: Aura Minerals (TSX: ORA) announced July 10 preliminary Q2 2026 production of 75,437 gold equivalent ounces across its six operating mines in Brazil, Mexico, Honduras, and the United States — an 18% improvement versus Q2 2025 and approximately 8% below Q1 2026, with the sequential decline reflecting planned maintenance and seasonal factors rather than operational deterioration. H1 2026 at approximately 157,250 GEO represents one of the company's strongest first-half periods since the multi-mine platform was assembled. Aura's six-mine, four-country diversification is its defining investment characteristic: no single asset dominates production, jurisdiction risk is distributed, and the portfolio generates operating cash flow across a wide band of gold prices. At $4,100+ gold, the H1 production run-rate implies significant free cash flow generation — the setup heading into Q2 financial results.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTHS RALLY IN JULY: 16.7% AVERAGE SURGE LED BY GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%
snippet: All 18 tracked rare earth elements posted price gains in July 2026, averaging 16.7% across the basket — led by germanium at +27.8% domestically, dysprosium +25.4%, and indium +26.5% — marking the broadest element-level rally of the current cycle and the second consecutive month of universal rare earth appreciation. The structural driver is a second consecutive year of supply deficit against EV motor, wind turbine, and defence electronics demand, amplified by the Trump administration's Project Vault: a $10 billion strategic reserve drawing on Export-Import Bank financing plus $2 billion in private capital, deploying with price-insensitive government purchasing power across the full critical minerals spectrum. For junior rare earth explorers on the TSXV and ASX, a sustained 16.7% monthly gain across the basket is the kind of fundamental backdrop that precedes major institutional re-rating of resource-stage companies — particularly those with dysprosium, terbium, and neodymium-bearing heavy rare earth profiles most insulated from Chinese export control risk.

headline: GOLDGROUP + GOLD RESOURCE $372M MEXICO MERGER CLEARS VOTE — FOUR-MINE PRECIOUS METALS PRODUCER CLOSING JULY 17
snippet: Shareholders of Goldgroup Mining Inc. and Gold Resource Corporation approved their US$372 million business combination on July 2, 2026, with the transaction targeting an on-schedule close on or about July 17. The merged company creates a multi-mine Mexico-focused precious metals producer spanning Goldgroup's Cerro Prieto mine and San Francisco project in Sonora plus Gold Resource's Don David mine in Oaxaca — alongside the Back Forty polymetallic development project in Michigan. With Goldgroup/Gold Resource closing July 17 and Equinox/Orla voting July 22, July is shaping up as the busiest month for precious metals M&A closings this cycle — a sign that majors and mid-tiers alike are using $4,100 gold to lock in valuations before the equity recovery that many analysts expect will follow the July 14 CPI print.

headline: LITHIUM FALLS 6.9% IN A MONTH AS CATL JIANXIAWO RESTARTS — SUPPLY WALL BUILDING AGAINST WEAK EV DEMAND
snippet: Lithium carbonate fell to 155,000 CNY per tonne — down 6.91% month-on-month despite trading 143% above its 2024–2025 lows — as CATL received security permit clearance to restart its Jianxiawo mine in China following a 10-month suspension, compounding supply pressure from Mineral Resources' Bald Hill restart in Western Australia (first spodumene concentrate expected July 2026) and Core Lithium's Finniss restart in the Northern Territory. Three simultaneous major restarts signal that current prices are sufficient to justify operating costs — but also that the supply shortfall driving the recovery is actively being addressed. The critical threshold: from here, price must be carried by demand rather than supply curtailment, but EV sales growth collapsed to 0.9% year-over-year in H1 2026 versus 20% for full-year 2025, and North American sales fell 25% after elimination of U.S. tax credits. Battery chemistry headwinds add further pressure — LFP chemistry now dominates Chinese autos and grid storage, containing neither cobalt nor nickel and limiting how much those metals benefit from the overall growth. Lithium equity investors face a supply-carries-more-weight market entering H2.

headline: MIDLAND EXPLORATION STARTS 3,500m DRILL AT WILLBOB GOLD — RIO TINTO, AGNICO, BARRICK ALL ON ADJACENT GROUND (TSXV:MD)
snippet: Midland Exploration Inc. (TSXV: MD) announced July 8 that drilling has commenced at its 100%-owned Willbob gold project in the Labrador Trough of Quebec — a 3,500-metre, 24-hole program targeting the Ants, Ferricrete, Pump Pad Ridge, Canyon, and Didgeridoo zones, with prior channel sampling at the Didgeridoo Zone returning 2.30 g/t Au over 8.95 metres including 3.56 g/t Au over 3.15 metres. The Labrador Trough is one of Quebec's most underexplored gold belts, and Midland's partner roster — Rio Tinto, Agnico Eagle, Barrick, Centerra, Wallbridge, and Fresnillo across various adjacent and related properties — provides the institutional endorsement signal that the district is geologically compelling. Midland's business model is systematic early-stage discovery that attracts major-company joint ventures; its track record of finding what majors then fund to resource makes a Midland drill start a reliable early-cycle signal for the Labrador Trough.

headline: COPPER $6.24/LB: UBS PROJECTS 520k-TONNE DEFICIT, COCHILCO RAISES FORECAST — MAJOR MINERS CUT GUIDANCE 199k TONNES
snippet: Copper traded at $6.24 per pound on July 10 as Chile's copper commission Cochilco raised its 2026 average price forecast in response to sustained supply underperformance and structural demand growth, joining Macquarie — which lifted its 2026 average to $13,165 per tonne from $12,310. UBS estimates a 2026 global refined copper deficit of 520,000 tonnes (demand growth 2.8% vs. supply growth 1.7%), while the 17 largest copper miners collectively cut 2026 production guidance by 199,000 tonnes to 13.8 million tonnes, with the largest disruptions at Kamoa-Kakula and Grasberg. For junior copper explorers with porphyry systems in stable jurisdictions — BC, Chile, Argentina — the combination of elevated spot price, tightening major-miner guidance, and institutional forecast upgrades represents the tightest copper supply-demand backdrop of the decade. Projects that were marginal at $3.50/lb are strongly economic at $6.24/lb, and the multi-year pipeline shortfall means first-production assets command premium valuations.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR STARTS 27,000-FOOT AURORA URANIUM DRILL — AMERICA'S LARGEST CONVENTIONAL MEASURED URANIUM RESOURCE
snippet: Nevada-based Eagle Nuclear Energy has commenced a 27,000-foot (8,230-metre) investigative drill program at its flagship Aurora Uranium Project along the Oregon-Nevada border, targeting completion in three to four months and a prefeasibility study by H2 2027. Aurora carries America's largest conventional measured and indicated uranium resource — a strategic distinction as the DOE commits $80 billion for new domestic reactors, the HALEU enrichment supply chain builds out, and the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act forces utilities to secure Western supply. The Aurora program advances directly toward PFS bankability: every metre drilled improves resource confidence for the feasibility study that precedes project financing. At $85.75/lb uranium with domestic supply receiving regulatory preference, Aurora's development timeline positions Eagle Nuclear among the rare group of near-term American uranium production candidates outside Wyoming in-situ recovery — a shorter list than the market currently prices.
